data.body:
Operator 2026-10-21 (verbatim): "Check for the same (as accrete) - pi.dev - research and see if it overlaps with ddflow, are there features we could pick on, and separately could we integrate with it"

Evidence: docs/ddflow/research/pi-dev.md (task PI-research) and research notes R-pidev-*.

VERDICT: Pi (pi.dev, github.com/earendil-works/pi, MIT, Earendil Inc.) is a minimal terminal coding-agent harness: a HARNESS ddflow should support, not a competitor and not a workflow tool (it deliberately ships no sub-agents, plan mode, permission popups, todos). It has a real TypeScript extension API (tool_call can block, agent_before_settle can continue, session_before_compact, input, session_start/shutdown), a built-in MCP client (stdio and streamable HTTP, list_changed honoured), print/JSON/RPC/SDK modes, reads AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md. Integration as a harness is MODERATE (extension template + descriptor + normalizer); as a lane worker over RPC EASY-TO-MODERATE; Pi consuming ddflow records needs nothing new (it reads the same instruction files and skills).

TRAPS found: (1) Pi MCP servers default to `codemode` exposure: ddflow's tools are NOT declared to the model unless the entry says `exposure: direct` (or `toolExposure`). (2) `.pi/extensions` and `.pi/mcp.json` load only after project trust; print/JSON/RPC modes silently skip them unless `--approve` or a saved decision, so a headless lane would have no ddflow. (3) `pi.exec` has no stdin option: hook payload to `ddflow hooks run` needs node:child_process. (4) Pi asks for no approval before tool calls; containment is ddflow's. (5) install telemetry defaults on.

ALREADY PLANNED, LINKED NOT RE-ADDED: pi descriptor = P-agent-parity.new-descriptors; stop-to-continue for Pi's plugin = P-agent-parity.continuation; plugin hook writer = P-agent-parity.kilo-plugin; lane launcher = P-agent-parity.launcher; ACP client/backend = P-acp; transcript import = B-am-ingest; per-client MCP profiles = MTD-profiles; per-client list_changed table = SU-client-table; docs-lift A/B = B-skills-adherence-eval.

WAVES: W1 PI-research (free, docs only) -> PI-decide (carries the P-gaps core/docs hold of D-old-work-behind-core-docs; everything below waits behind it). W2 (parallel, disjoint globs) PI-facts, PI-normalizer, PI-client-row, PI-session-ingest. W3 PI-extension, PI-exposure-map, PI-onboard-verify, PI-lane-rpc. W4 PI-lane-events. W5 PI-e2e. W6 PI-docs.
data.title: Pi (pi.dev) fit: Pi as a supported harness (extension, MCP exposure, trust), as a lane worker over RPC/JSON, session ingest, and the generic gaps it exposes

data.body: Ask the operator (AskUserQuestion) and file docs/ddflow/decisions/pi-dev.md. Questions: (1) Direction order: harness first, lane worker second, session ingest third; or harness only. (2) May adopt write an executable TypeScript extension into .pi/extensions (runs in Pi's process with the user's permissions, loads only after project trust), or only ship it as a Pi package the operator installs with `pi install`? (3) Gate hooks fail closed (Pi's own rule: a throwing tool_call handler blocks the tool) or open (ddflow missing must not brick the session)? Recommendation: closed for claim/lease enforcement only when ddflow answered 'refuse'; ddflow unreachable is `unavailable`, recorded, not a block. (4) Telemetry: Pi's enableInstallTelemetry defaults to true; may ddflow set it false in lane config? (5) Tier for Pi in D-agent-compat (headless smoke needs a provider key; Pi supports 15+ providers, so which). (6) Minimum Pi version floor. Carries the hold of D-old-work-behind-core-docs for the whole phase (the P-gaps core and the docs wave).
data.title: Operator decisions: Pi support tier and scope, installing an in-process extension, fail-open or fail-closed gates, what leaves the machine

data.body: Normalizer and emitter for the "pi" dialect in the hook core (ddflow/services/hookcore/pi.py). Pi has no command-hook protocol: the extension (PI-extension) sends one JSON object on stdin to `ddflow hooks run --harness pi <event>`, so ddflow defines it. Event map: session_start -> session_start; input -> prompt; tool_call -> pre_tool; tool_result -> post_tool; session_before_compact -> pre_compact (handoff); agent_before_settle -> stop; session_shutdown -> session_end. Payload carries Pi session id (ctx.sessionManager), cwd, tool name and input, and the Pi version (for drift). Answers: {block, reason} for pre_tool, {message} for session_start/prompt injection, {continue, prompt} for stop. Fixtures are recorded from a real Pi when installed, else marked recorded:false. Conformance run per docs/ddflow/adding-a-harness.md. ddflow unreachable or timing out is answered by the extension as unavailable, per PI-decide.
data.title: hooks run --harness pi: normalise Pi extension payloads and emit answers (block with reason, injected context, continue), with recorded fixtures

data.body: Pi's default exposure for an MCP server is `codemode`: tools are callable from scripts but not declared to the model, so a plain `pi mcp add ddflow` leaves the model without ddflow_brief/claim. Adopt writes the .pi/mcp.json (or user file) entry with `exposure` and a `toolExposure` map derived from the MTD-profiles tier list: loop tools (brief, next, claim, heartbeat, gate_status, merge, complete, recall) `direct`, the rest `deferred` (found by tool_search) or `codemode`, destructive ones `hidden` unless the operator allows; plus a one-line `description` (it lists the server in Pi's system prompt). Needs a descriptor [mcp] entry_extra table (one definition, owned here, coordinated with descriptor-v2). Doctor reads the effective config and reports `model_cannot_see_ddflow` when the server is codemode/hidden and tool_search/codemode are inactive. Generalises to any client with native tiering; the Pi mapping is the first user. Pi tool names are mcp__ddflow__<tool>, same shape as Claude Code, so ddflow's name-based hints stay valid.
data.title: Write the ddflow MCP entry for Pi with exposure direct for the loop tools (client-native tiering) and a doctor check that the model can actually see ddflow

data.body: Steps for `ddflow harness verify pi` (P-agent-lifecycle.verify): (1) `pi --version` against the floor from PI-decide; (2) `pi mcp list --json` (Pi's own probe: exit 1 when an entry is invalid or an enabled server is not connected) shows ddflow connected and its tool count; (3) project trust: read [REDACTED:path] and defaultProjectTrust (read-only, never written); with no saved decision, print/JSON/RPC modes skip .pi/extensions and .pi/mcp.json, so the hooks step is `unavailable: project not trusted` and a lane must start with --approve (PI-lane-rpc); (4) the extension file digest against the manifest (P-agent-lifecycle.manifest). pi missing from PATH or a probe that cannot run is unavailable, never passed.
data.title: Verify Pi onboarding for real: pi mcp list --json, project-trust state, version floor; a silently skipped extension is unavailable, not done

data.body: Descriptor [headless] and a launch template for the lane launcher, native RPC backend (AC-prefer: native beats acp for Pi; the community pi-acp adapters wrap this same RPC and are REPORTED, not needed). Command: pi --mode rpc --session-id <lane-session> --approve with PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR pointing at a lane-private agent dir (no user credentials by default; provider key passed by env, never argv), cwd = the lane worktree. Protocol facts: JSONL on stdin/stdout, strict LF framing (not readline), stdout reserved for records; prompt response means accepted, completion is `agent_settled` (not `agent_end`); steer and follow_up commands map to AC-steer; abort; get_state gives sessionId/sessionFile for the ledger; close stdin for orderly stop; `--mode json` for one-shot jobs (a failed assistant response there does NOT set a non-zero exit, so the lane reads stopReason). No permission prompts exist in Pi, so containment is ddflow's (worktree-only cwd, AC-permissions policy cannot intercept: use the extension's tool_call gate or an OS sandbox). Missing pi, missing provider key, or an untrusted project is unavailable. --offline and enableInstallTelemetry=false per PI-decide.
data.title: Pi as a lane worker: launch template for pi --mode rpc / --mode json, completion on agent_settled, steer and follow_up, abort, session id, MCP injection with --approve

data.body: ddflow/templates/harness/pi/ddflow.ts, written by adopt into .pi/extensions/ddflow/ (also laid out as a Pi package: package.json with `pi` key and `pi-package` keyword, so `pi install git:...` works; publishing is a PI-decide item). Uses node:child_process to run `ddflow hooks run --harness pi <event>` with a JSON stdin payload, because pi.exec has no stdin option. Handlers: session_start -> inject the brief through before_agent_start (a returned message, so the system prompt and its cache are untouched); input -> prompt capture (ddflow session prompt); tool_call -> pre_tool, returns {block:true, reason} when ddflow refuses (claim or lease missing, write outside the lease globs); tool_result -> post_tool monitoring; session_before_compact -> handoff note (B-am-handoff); agent_before_settle -> asks the continuation engine and returns continue:true with the next prompt, guarded by max_consecutive (Pi warns an unconditional continuation loops); session_shutdown -> session_end, idempotent. Every handler has a timeout; a ddflow failure is recorded unavailable per PI-decide. Idempotent install, revertable, manifest entry, pinned to the Pi version range of PI-facts. Does nothing in sessions without a ddflow project.
data.title: The ddflow Pi extension template (TypeScript) adopt installs: session start brief, prompt capture, tool gate, compaction handoff, stop-to-continue

data.body: Pi event -> ddflow event through the registry: tool_execution_start args (read/edit/write/bash) -> paths touched for lease and glob conflict detection (a write outside the lease is a conflict event); message_end usage/cost -> meters (UNAVAILABLE when not reported); compaction_start/compaction_end (reason manual|threshold|overflow, tokensBefore, estimatedTokensAfter) -> context meter and handoff trigger; auto_retry_* -> lane health; agent_end vs agent_settled -> lane 'turn done' vs 'lane idle' (the settled distinction is the one ddflow's continuation engine and AC-turn-loop need: end_turn alone is not final); queue_update -> steering backlog; extension_error -> attention item. message_update deltas are dropped from the log (kept only as a bounded tail), the session JSONL stays the full record. Reader honours stdout backpressure and LF framing.
data.title: Map Pi's JSONL events to ddflow lane events: tool paths for lease conflict, usage, compaction, settled; bounded and spilled

data.body: A scripted fake pi (stdio JSONL, scripted events incl. agent_settled, configurable version, trust state, exposure) under tests/fixtures/fake_pi/. Scenarios: (a) claim -> brief -> gates -> merge -> complete driven through the fake lane with steer and follow_up; (b) a tool_call outside the lease blocks and logs a conflict; (c) untrusted project: extension and mcp skipped, verify says unavailable, lane started with --approve works; (d) ddflow server entry with exposure codemode: doctor reports model_cannot_see_ddflow; (e) pi missing, bad JSON line, stdout garbage, crash mid-turn, huge update stream, provider key absent: unavailable recorded, no gate passes; (f) compaction mid-lane produces a handoff and the session import is incremental; (g) a prompt-injection string in a tool result stays fenced as imported. Marks the live headless smoke as a skipped, recorded gap when pi is not installed (D-agent-compat tiering).
data.title: End-to-end with a fake Pi: hooks, lane over RPC, trust skip, exposure, session import; failures are unavailable, never a pass

data.claim: pi.dev is Pi, a minimal, MIT-licensed terminal coding-agent harness by Earendil Inc. (github.com/earendil-works/pi, package @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent 1.3.0), with interactive, print, JSON, RPC and SDK modes, reading AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md; it deliberately ships no sub-agents, plan mode, permission popups or todos.
data.falsifier: A LICENSE other than MIT, or a core feature list that includes built-in sub-agents or permission prompts.
data.mechanism: Extensions, skills, prompt templates and packages supply what the core omits.

data.question: What is pi.dev, who makes it, is it open source, and is it a coding agent harness?

data.claim: `pi --mode rpc` is a documented JSONL stdin/stdout protocol (prompt, steer, follow_up, abort, get_state with sessionId/sessionFile, get_entries with a since cursor, compact, fork) whose completion signal is agent_settled, not agent_end; `--mode json` streams the same events for one-shot runs but a failed assistant response does not set a non-zero exit status. No permission prompts exist, so containment must come from ddflow or the OS. Whether it is robust under long unattended runs is UNKNOWN (never run).
data.falsifier: A live run where agent_settled is missing after retries, or rpc-commands.md lacking steer/follow_up.
data.mechanism: Same agent and session code behind all modes.
data.probe: none run: docs read only (rpc.md, rpc-commands.md, json.md, cli-integration.md, environment-variables.md); the code was not executed on this machine
